summary: Batched normalization discrepancy causing rerank order flip and streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a recent client upgrade (MediumCorp Data Platform v2.5) resulted in rerank responses whose top-k ordering flips intermittently and which sometimes stream blank/partial responses then time out. The customer uses our dedicated deployment in us-east and runs their own batching layer in front of the embeddings API.

Impact:
- Observed order instability in production queries affecting relevance-sensitive features (search and recommendations).
- Occasional streaming timeouts on rerank endpoint with 504s after token stream stalls for ~8-12s.
- Customer business impact: A/B tests show CTR drop ~6% on search page for affected cohort.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer subnet) in prod:us-east, fallbacks to eu-west for cross-region traffic.
- Client: MediumCorp Data Platform v2.5 (uses client-sdk v3.2 with batched embedding calls and explicit L2-normalization client-side).
- Server models: rwd-embed-1-small (embeddings), rwd-rerank-2 (reranker).

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Construct a 50-query batch at 200 qps via their batching layer to /v1/embeddings with normalize=true on the client.
2) Send the resulting vector batch to /v1/rerank with per-item metadata and expect top-5 ordered scores.
3) Observe that in ~5-10% of batches, rerank returns an ordering where items with identical content flip positions between requests; streaming path returns partial tokens then stalls to timeout.

Observed logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Example payloads (sanitized) showing embedding vectors of length 384 and some vectors containing trailing zeros for ~30% of items in certain batches.
- Client debug shows it calls client-sdk.normalizeBatch(vectors) before sending; server side logs show Accept-Encoding: chunked and several "stream-write timeout" events around the rerank worker PID.
- Sample timestamps: 2026-03-11T15:23:01.123Z batch-id=mc-9912 - rerank stream stall after token 12 of 45.

Initial hypothesis:
- Mismatch between client-side normalization and server-side expectation (server expects unit-normalized embedding when computing cosine similarity inside reranker). Batched client normalization + internal batch-padding/truncation could produce slightly different floating point distributions, and occasional trailing-zero padding from the customer's batching layer is being interpreted as valid vector data. That leads to near-duplicate vectors with changed magnitudes, which both perturbs ranking and occasionally triggers the streaming path to fall back/mis-handle KV cache offsets, causing stream stalls.

Requested from customer:
- Full raw batch (pre-normalization) and post-normalization vectors for three failing batches.
- Network captures around the chunked stream difference.
- Confirmation of exact client-sdk version and any custom patch to normalization routine.

Priority/SLAs:
- P1 / Sev1 due to direct revenue impact (CTR and search regressions). First response SLA met. Working with customer success on daily syncs.
comments: 2026-03-13 10:02 - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledged ticket and requested raw embeddings and sample request IDs. Escalated to L2 rerank team.
2026-03-13 13:45 - MediumCorp (Customer): Uploaded three failing batches (mc-9912, mc-9940, mc-10012). Noted they do call normalizeBatch and that they recently upgraded client-sdk.

2026-03-13 15:17 - Liam O'Connor (Rerank Eng): Preliminary check: saw trailing zeros in ~34% of vectors in mc-9912. Opening a short-term mitigation to detect zero-trailing vectors and rewrite to NaN/invalid to force client re-send. Filing PR to add server-side validation.

2026-03-14 09:12 - SRE (Helena Zhou): Observed a correlation between chunk size and stream stall windows. When batch encoding crosses 16KB boundary, rerank streaming writes sometimes block under high contention. Investigating connection buffer thresholds.

2026-03-14 11:30 - Liam O'Connor: Added instrumentation to log vector-norm before similarity computation and to increment metric 'rerank.invalid_vector_detected'. Deployed hotfix to dedicated pool for MediumCorp to reject vectors with trailing zeros and return 400 with guidance.

2026-03-14 12:05 - MediumCorp: Confirmed that after temporary hotfix their failing batches now receive a 400 with detail indicating 'trailing_zero_padding_detected' and are working on fixing client-side batching. Customer requests permanent fix to co-exist with client-side normalization differences.

2026-03-14 12:45 - Product (Sofia Martinez): Requesting design doc for server-side resilient normalization and clear API contract (server expects unit vectors unless header 'raw-embeddings: true' set).
investigation_notes: 1) Reproducer built using the customer's client-sdk v3.2 + a small shim that pads batches to multiples of 8 causing trailing zeros. Confirmed rank flips when padded zeros are present and when server does not re-normalize. 2) Rerank code historically assumed incoming vectors are normalized; defensive checks were minimal to avoid extra CPU. 3) Streaming stall reproduced when chunked response hit internal write buffer limit while a goroutine performing KV lookup experienced GC pauses; combination caused stream writer to block and client to time out. 4) Metric spike: rerank.invalid_vector_detected=128 in 24h window for customer pool. 5) No sign of model weight corruption or quantization mismatch (scores scaled normally).
proposed_fix: Short term: server hotfix to validate vectors and return explicit 400 with 'trailing_zero_padding_detected' and a remediation message. Medium term: implement server-side optional renormalization flow when header 'x-allow-renorm: true' is provided; add best-effort trimming of all-zero suffix bytes in embedding payloads and log telemetry. Long term: update public API docs and client-sdk to avoid silent normalization semantics mismatch, add pre-flight validation endpoint /v1/embeddings/validate. Also add integration test to CI that simulates batched padding patterns.
resolution: In progress - temporary validation hotfix deployed to MediumCorp's dedicated pool on 2026-03-14 11:30. Customer confirmed hotfix surfaced explicit 400s and they are rolling a client patch to stop appending padding zeros. Engineering to deliver medium-term renormalization option and docs updates. No full RCA posted yet; follow-up postmortem scheduled after deploy of medium-term fix.
notes_for_follow_up:
- Track metric 'rerank.invalid_vector_detected' for customer pool for 7 days.
- Schedule API contract clarification in next sprint; owner: Sofia Martinez.
- SRE to review streaming write buffer defaults and GC tuning for dedicated pools.
- Communicate to SDK teams to add explicit warnings when normalize=true is used with batched padding.
